templates.title: Implementation Plan
templates.when_to_use: Lay out the phases of a planned change, the files each phase touches, and the order they land in. Reach for it when a reviewer needs the shape of the work before they read any code.

templates.title: Spec Explainer
templates.when_to_use: Explain what a feature does and why it is being built, for a reader who has not opened the spec. Reach for it when the change is easier to judge from its intent than from its diff.

templates.title: Code Approaches
templates.when_to_use: Put two or more implementation approaches side by side with the trade-off that decides between them. Reach for it when planning weighed a real alternative and the reviewer needs to see why the chosen one won.

templates.title: Module Map
templates.when_to_use: Map the existing modules a change touches and how they call each other. Reach for it when the change edits code a reviewer has to understand before they can read the edit.

templates.title: Pull Request Write-up
templates.when_to_use: State what the finished change does, what it deliberately leaves out, and how it was verified. Reach for it on any pull request you are asking someone to review.

templates.title: Annotated Diff
templates.when_to_use: Walk a reviewer through the diff hunk by hunk, annotating the ones that need it. Reach for it when the change is large, or when the self-review recorded a gap worth pointing at.

templates.title: Flowchart
templates.when_to_use: Draw a multi-step process as a diagram: the steps, the branches, and the points where it can fail. Reach for it when the change alters a runtime or delivery flow that prose describes poorly.

templates.title: UAT Walkthrough
templates.when_to_use: Give a non-engineer numbered steps to run against the change, each with an observable result and a pass or fail toggle, and export the outcome as text. Reach for it when acceptance depends on someone exercising the change rather than reading it.

templates.title: Visual Design Options
templates.when_to_use: Show several visual directions for the same screen so a reader can choose one. Reach for it before any of them is built.

templates.title: Design System
templates.when_to_use: Document the tokens, type scale, and components a surface is built from, each rendered as itself. Reach for it when contributors need one place to check what a color or a spacing step is called.

templates.title: Component Variants
templates.when_to_use: Render every state of one component on a single page: default, hover, focus, disabled, error, and loading. Reach for it when a state is easy to miss and expensive to get wrong.

templates.title: Animation Prototype
templates.when_to_use: Play a motion design at real speed so timing and easing can be judged rather than described. Reach for it when a still image cannot settle the question.

templates.title: Interaction Prototype
templates.when_to_use: Make a flow clickable so a reader can walk it themselves. Reach for it when the open question is how a sequence of steps behaves, not how one screen looks.

templates.title: SVG Illustrations
templates.when_to_use: Draw a diagram or illustration as vector markup that stays sharp at any size and loads no image file. Reach for it when the picture carries the explanation.

templates.title: Slide Deck
templates.when_to_use: Present a finding as paged slides you step through while people watch. Reach for it when the audience is listening rather than reading.

templates.title: Concept Explainer
templates.when_to_use: Teach one unfamiliar concept from first principles, with a worked example. Reach for it when the reader needs the idea itself before they can use anything built on it.

templates.title: Status Report
templates.when_to_use: Report where work stands: what landed, what is in flight, what is blocked, and on whom. Reach for it for a recurring update where the reader wants the state rather than the narrative.

templates.title: Incident Report
templates.when_to_use: Record what broke, when it broke, what the impact was, and what stops it recurring. Reach for it after an outage or a defect that reached users.

templates.title: Triage Board
templates.when_to_use: Sort a list of issues into columns, then export the result as text you can paste back. Reach for it when triage decisions have to leave the page in a form another tool reads.

templates.title: Feature Flag Editor
templates.when_to_use: Toggle a set of flags and export the configuration that results. Reach for it when someone needs to compose a flag state without hand-editing the config file.

templates.title: Prompt Tuner
templates.when_to_use: Edit a prompt beside its output, compare revisions, and export the version you keep. Reach for it when a prompt is being tuned by hand and each change has to be seen.
